Caution

Spoiler warning. Participants: stop here. This page names the records the reference review included, the traps in each extraction paper and the expected AI errors. Reading it before you have saved your own screening and extraction makes the exercise meaningless. Go back to the activity guide. If you are doing the exercise on your own, come back after step 3: the sections "What to expect in screening", "What to expect in extraction" and "Interpreting the scores" are then your debrief.

For the people running the hands-on part of the seminar, at EPH 2026 in Bilbao (Thursday 12 November 2026, 16:45-17:45) or in a later run of the same workshop. Participants use README.md; this page adds timing, preparation, the pitfalls you should expect, and how to run the debrief. Do not project it.

Status of the answers. The reference review was confirmed by the workshop team on 6 November 2026 (see data/README.md). The extraction reference values were prepared by the workshop team from the full texts, each with a verbatim quote and, where available, the reference review's own table entry (review_table_value); they have not yet been validated against the review team's extraction sheet. Say so when participants compare with them.

What we learned in Berlin (Sept 2026)#

A longer version of this workshop ran at the EUPHA DHAI annual meeting in Berlin on 10 September 2026 (27 participants): building and critiquing a search strategy with an LLM, then data extraction. About half of the participants used ChatGPT and half Claude; a few used Gemini, Perplexity or Consensus. From the session notes and the Mentimeter poll:

What happened in Berlin What we changed for Bilbao
A ChatGPT Pro chat with internet access recognised the recently published reference review and asked whether the participant wanted to repeat exactly that research Rule 1 for everyone: web search / browsing off and a temporary chat (memory off); the prompts say "do not search the web". Pruna et al. 2026 is published too
Most participants used zero-shot prompts without instructions (mainly those with an IT background added them) Ready-to-paste prompts with the criteria C1-C6, the rules and the output format already filled in
Not enough time to check the outputs themselves; the AI's search strategy "seems solid at first" Fewer tasks (20 records, 1 paper, 5 fields) and a whole step (step 2) for verifying, with a verifier checklist
The LLM's critique listed many possible errors; checking and ranking them meant reading the whole long answer Prompts ask for short, ranked output: a CSV with reasons of at most 25 words; the top three risks in the search critique (prompt 2.2)
Terms needed human context: which infections count as healthcare-associated? Which AI technologies are included? Explicit criteria C1-C6 from the reference review; C5 lists the HAI outcomes that count
Extraction: some found it useful; others said it made quite some assumptions and would use it only for straightforward categories Step 3 uses 5 straightforward fields, each with a verbatim quote and its location, and not reported as an allowed answer
The reproducibility of the LLM was discussed a lot, and also that of humans: how reproducible are human scientists? A study comparing the two was named as a need A second run in a new chat (Going further, kappa in the scorer); "How reproducible are human reviewers?" in the discussion; the research idea under Going further
What worked: the demonstration, step-by-step instructions, practical examples, the choice of individual or group work. One participant found it "too complicated for me" A demo video of the three steps with captions that name every button, commented live (the demo in four hands as fallback); the Start page with the three steps in order; individual work, comparing with a neighbour optional; the beginners track (learning only)

Confidence at the end (23 of 27 answered; the sliders have no numeric scale labels): 3.6 on the strongly disagree–strongly agree slider that their LLM-built search strategy would find the relevant literature, and 3 that their extraction form would hold up on a paper they had not seen yet.

Demo script#

Ten minutes, 16:55-17:05, Francesco Baglivo and Patrick Boudreau together. The demo is a video, commented live: docs/assets/demo/demo.mp4 (4:53, silent, captions burned in; also on the Start page and embedded in the slides). It shows the three steps exactly as the participants will do them, with the same step names and button labels, on demo material (batch 3 and Mestre2012), with real AI answers recorded on 6 November 2026 (an AI chat assistant, the prompts of the site, web search off; details and the raw answers in demo/README.md). The message is the same as in the live version: one drives the AI, one checks the source, and the errors are caught by the verifier, not by the AI.

  • Francesco narrates what the AI is asked to do and what it answers ("the prompt already has C1-C6", "the AI says 20 rows").

  • Patrick speaks for the verifier: "show me where it says that". He reads the highlighted sentence aloud and says what is accepted.

  • Let the captions carry the instructions; do not read them out. Pause the video (space bar) only at the three recap cards if the room needs it.

Video On screen Francesco (narrates) Patrick (verifier)
0:00 Title, the three steps "Five minutes, then it is your turn: same steps, your own laptop." "Batch 3 and Mestre2012 here; you get batch 1 and Phan2020."
0:18 Step 1 · Screening: records, prompt, chat "Records page, batch 3, Copy batch. Start page, Copy the screening prompt." "Web search off, temporary chat. Exclude only when the abstract clearly says so."
1:09 The AI's answer "This is what the AI returned, unedited." "Before reading a single decision: 20 records in, 20 rows out? We count."
1:26 Scorer "Paste it all, Score my screening." "Coverage first. Then missed includes: zero here. That is the costly error."
1:50 Step 2 · Look at the errors "4 false includes, all excluded by the review only after reading the full text." "Not errors at this stage. But look: the AI excluded 3 records the human screeners kept. Check its excludes too."
2:25 R050 and R058 on the Records page "The AI's reason is the blue box. We read the abstract instead." R050: "Hospital-wide campaign, infections only in the ICU: unsure is fair." R058: "Components not described, then contact precautions and bathing: C3 in doubt."
3:28 Step 3 · Short extraction "Copy prompt + this paper: one paste." "A value without a quote is not a value."
4:01 Quotes in the full text "Show text, then find the quote." Quote 1: "Word for word, in the affiliations: the form allows it if the location says so." Quote 2: "Word for word, but the number in the value is not in the quote. Found it in Table 1, a few lines up. Check every number."
4:43 Your turn Hands over: "Your turn. Start page, step 1." "Today, on your own, you do both: you drive the AI, then you verify it."

After the video (about 17:01): the participants open the Start page on their own laptop; Francesco switches to the whiteboard slide and writes the three points the verifier caught in the video (3 excludes stricter than the human screeners; R058 include with a doubt on C3; a number not in its quote), to be completed with the participants' errors in the discussion.

Fallback: the live demo in four hands#

If the video cannot be played (no sound is needed, but a broken file or a projector that cannot show video can happen), run the demo live, in four hands, with exactly the same steps, as below.

  • Francesco = driver. At the keyboard. Runs the AI with exactly the pages and prompts the participants will use, and says aloud what he clicks.

  • Patrick = verifier. Never touches the AI. Asks "show me where it says that" and checks the answers against the abstract or the paper. He decides what is accepted.

Today, on your own, you do both: participants then run the same steps alone, first as driver, then as verifier (see Working on your own). The point to land at the end: the errors were caught by the verifier, not by the AI.

Pages used. All on the published site, https://fraba94.github.io/eph2026-ai-for-evidence-synthesis/ (or on http://localhost:8000/ if you serve docs/ from a laptop):

  • Start page, start.html: the screening prompt with C1-C6 already pasted in, with a Copy button.
  • Records page, batch.html: the batches; missing abstracts are filled from PubMed in the browser.

  • Papers page, papers.html: the full texts (Copy, Download, Show) and the short extraction prompt with the 5 fields already filled in; on the Mestre2012 card, Copy prompt + this paper gives the prompt with study_id = Mestre2012 and the paper already pasted in. The 11-field version is under "Going further". Same prompts in the beginners walkthrough, step 4 and the prompt library (3.1, 4.2).

  • Scorer, scorer.html: paste the AI's answer as it is; nothing is uploaded.

  • Answers page, answers.html: screening answers after step 1, extraction answers after step 3, each behind its own button.
  • Mestre2012 full text (CC BY 4.0), the demo paper: data/fulltext/Mestre2012.txt, or as plain text to select all and copy.

Important

Demo on batch 3 (R041-R060), not batch 1. The chat-track participants screen batch 1 (R001-R020) right after the demo: projecting the scorer on batch 1 would show them its missed includes. Batch 3 keeps the same steps without the spoiler (agent-track participants, who screen all 60, see 20 of their answers: tell them so). Likewise, the demo extracts Mestre2012, not Phan2020: the chat-track participants extract Phan2020 right after.

What to watch for#

Part Patrick looks for What it shows
A. Screening Missing or renamed rows: fewer than 20 rows, an ID skipped or repeated, R41 instead of R041, rows out of order Chat assistants drop rows silently; the self-reported count can be wrong
A. Screening A reason that cites no criterion (no C1-C6 code), or a rule that is not in the criteria ("small sample", "low quality", "not in Europe") The model adds its own criteria
A. Screening Exclude when the abstract is silent (the reason says "not mentioned", "unclear", "no information") At this stage that is unsure, not exclude: a possible missed include
B. Extraction A quote that is not in the paper (Ctrl+F finds nothing, or finds a near-identical sentence) Invented or paraphrased quote: the value is unverified
B. Extraction A number that is not in its quote (the value says one figure, the quote another or none) The value came from somewhere else, or was computed or rounded
B. Extraction A false "not reported" (Ctrl+F on a synonym finds it, often in a table) Missed information: "not reported" must be checked like any other value

The day before#

  • Network. Open start.html, batch.html (batch 3 fills its abstracts) and scorer.html on the venue Wi-Fi, or on the phone hotspot you will use as a fallback.

  • Chat assistant. Logged in on the demo laptop; web search / browsing off and a temporary chat (memory off); no project knowledge or custom instructions that could leak earlier runs. Show the participants where you switched web search off: it is the first of their three rules.

  • Readable from the back of the room. Browser zoom 150%, large font in the chat; dark mode off if the projector washes it out.

  • Two tabs open: start.html and the chat. Keep batch.html, scorer.html and Mestre2012.txt one click away (a local copy of Mestre2012.txt works without network).

  • Extraction prompt ready: the short extraction prompt for Mestre2012 (Papers page, Mestre2012 card, Copy prompt + this paper), also saved in a text file on the laptop as a backup.

  • Rehearsal run saved locally as backup, in case the live run shows no error or the network fails: the screening CSV, the extraction CSV and screenshots of the chat and of the scorer, with one error marked. Keep it on the laptop only (outside the repository or in the git-ignored activity/data/local/): do not commit or post outputs that contain copyrighted abstracts.

  • AI use record. Note the model name, version and date of the rehearsal, and again on the day, in the AI use record (optional for participants, under "Going further"): the demo shows what to record.

  • Rehearse the commentary on the video once, with the table of the demo script; then the fallback once in four hands with a timer: who speaks when, and where the hand-over at 9:15 happens.

If something fails#

Problem What to do
The video does not play (slides or browser) Play the local copy of docs/assets/demo/demo.mp4 in another player, or open it from the Start page; if none works, run the live demo in four hands
No network (records page, chat or scorer do not load) Show the saved rehearsal run: screenshots of the chat, the CSV and the scorer. Say it is a rehearsal and when it was run. Then point participants to the fallbacks
The AI makes no visible error Say so: it is also a result, and it does not prove the next run will be clean. Show the rehearsal's error and who caught it
Records page does not fill the abstracts Use the records shipped with abstracts (see If things go wrong) or the rehearsal run
Time overrun Skip part B (extraction). Always keep part C: the errors on the whiteboard and the hand-over

What to expect in screening#

Record IDs refer to the current build (seed 2026). Chat-track participants see R001-R020 (4 includes).

Record(s) Reference Typical AI behaviour and why it is instructive
R003 (multicentre programme, Chicago), R022 (national Cleanyourhands campaign), R017 (automated monitoring plus promotion), R040 (7-hospital system, CLABSI), R060 (Targeted Solutions Tool) include Often missed: the outcome is antimicrobial resistance or an association with HAI (C5 looks weak), the setting is national or a health system (C1/C2 look odd), or electronic monitoring triggers the "single measure" exclusion in C3 although it is embedded in a wider strategy
R039 (hospital-wide programme, Geneva) exclude, flagged Appears to meet all criteria but is not among the review's included or full-text-excluded studies: possible gold-standard error. Use it to ask "who checks the reference?"
R007, R009, R051 (single neonatal ICU), R045 (single urology ward) exclude Include-looking abstracts with HAI outcomes: the AI must apply C2 (single unit). Good test of whether the criteria were pasted verbatim
R005, R015 and other bundles exclude Hand hygiene appears in the abstract, but as one component of MRSA/CRE/HAI bundles: C3 requires judgement; unsure is acceptable at this stage
R034, R047 (randomised trials) exclude Strong designs excluded by C4: participants are often surprised, which is a good moment to say that criteria are the review's choice, not the AI's
R023 (equine hospitals) exclude Tests whether anyone (human or AI) reads past the title
The 21 records the review excluded after full text (e.g. R013, R020, R031, R046, R050, R054) exclude (final) Including them at title/abstract stage is correct behaviour; the scorer's "title/abstract-stage view" counts them as include
Any batch - Rows dropped, renamed IDs, decisions without a criterion, exclude used instead of unsure, long batches where middle records get shorter reasons

What to expect in extraction#

All three papers contain traps that come from the papers, not from the AI. The notes column of answers/extraction_gold.csv explains each one.

Paper Pitfall What a careful extraction does
Phan2020 Post-intervention compliance 75.1% in the text, 75.0% in Table 1; Table 1 title says 2010-2016 but runs to 2018 Quotes the text value and notices the table difference
Phan2020 HAI outcome called "overall HAI" in Results, "HAI other than SSI" in the Discussion and in the reference review Names the outcome as the authors define it in Methods
Phan2020 IRR 0.85 is a per-year trend, not a before-after ratio Says what the estimate measures
Phan2020 Concurrent CAUTI programme and SSI measures Reports co-interventions instead of "none"
Mestre2012 The country appears only in the author affiliations ("Delfos Medical Center, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain"); Methods mention only a "Catalonian Regional Campaign" Spain with the affiliation quote and "author affiliations" as location is correct. Spain with no quote, or with a quote that is not in the paper, is an inference to verify. The PDF and the text file both contain the affiliations
Mestre2012 The HAI outcome (MRSA) is secondary; the primary outcome is compliance Does not report compliance as the HAI outcome
Mestre2012 MRSA rates shown only in a control chart: no numbers in the text not reported for baseline and post rates; numbers "read" from the figure are not in the text
Mestre2012 Baseline period given three ways (March 2007, October 2007, 2007-2008); phase 1 compliance 78% in Table 2 but 79.5% in the Abstract, with a CI that does not contain 78; denominator per 1,000 in Methods vs per 10,000 in Results Flags internal inconsistencies
AlKuwaiti2017 Post-intervention HAI rate 2.59 (Abstract, Results), 2.5483 (Table II, 2016) and 2.55 (Discussion); which year was the intervention year is not stated Quotes one value and its location, notes the others
AlKuwaiti2017 No surveillance definition; no effect estimate (only P < 0.05); a non-significant correlation (r = -0.278, p = 0.381) easily reported as an "effect" not reported where the paper is silent
AlKuwaiti2017 Licence CC BY-NC: not shipped in the repository Agent track fetches it locally; chat track uses Phan2020 (Mestre2012 at home)

Interpreting the scores#

  • Coverage first. The scorer starts with "Screened N of 60 records" and lists records not screened. Metrics are computed on the screened records; the line "Sensitivity counting not-screened includes as missed" shows the cost of dropped records (chat assistants often drop rows). Agent-track participants should score with --expect-all.

  • Sensitivity first. At title/abstract stage, a missed include is the costly error. Precision against the final decision is naturally low because 21 records reached the review's full-text stage: point participants to the title/abstract-stage view and to gold_basis.

  • Kappa between two runs (going further) shows sampling variability: the same prompt, the same records, different answers. Ask what a reviewer would report about it.

  • Extraction: QUOTE NOT FOUND (invented or paraphrased quote), unsupported (value where the paper is silent) and false absent (missed information, often in tables) matter more than small numeric differences. within tol. values deserve a look (e.g. 2.55 vs 2.59 in AlKuwaiti2017 are two different numbers of the same paper).

  • The reference can be wrong. R039; the review's Table 1 citing "Larson et al., 2010" for a 2000 paper; values that differ between the abstract, the text and the tables of the same paper (all three extraction papers). Treat a discrepancy as a question for the source, not a verdict on the AI.

Debrief prompts (last 10 minutes)#

Start with the errors: each person brings one error they found (step 2 or step 3), and it goes on the whiteboard slide of the demo next to the errors the verifier caught. Then:

  1. Performance. Hands up: whose AI missed at least one include? Which one, and why?
  2. Transparency. Who found a quote that was not in the paper? How long did it take to find out?

  3. Bias. Were the errors random, or always the same kind (single units, bundles, numbers in tables, inferred countries)?

  4. Oversight. Who would sign the extraction table as it came out of the AI? What would you need to check first?

  5. Reproducibility. Who tried a second run (going further)? Did it agree? And how reproducible are human reviewers: would two of you agree on the same paper? What should go in a methods section so that someone can repeat it?
  6. The reference. Did anyone disagree with the reference after checking the source?

Close with the repository's position: these tools can help people who understand how they work and verify them systematically; for everyone else the beginners track is for learning only, not for real reviews.

If things go wrong#

Problem Fallback
Network blocks NCBI (records page cannot fill abstracts) Use the 17 records shipped with abstracts: R008, R011, R018 (the only ones in batch 1), R021, R023, R029, R032, R034, R035, R038, R041, R046, R052, R053, R054, R056, R058; or share the local screening_records_full.csv on the facilitator laptop screen (do not post it online)
Chat assistant refuses uploads Paste the text from data/fulltext/Phan2020.txt in two halves, in the same conversation
Someone is fast Going further: a second run in a new chat; the 11 core fields; the second paper (Mestre2012); the agent track on all 60 records
Someone is slow Screen 10 records only (batch size 10 on the records page); if step 3 does not fit, keep the error found in step 2 for the discussion
Published website (GitHub Pages) not available Serve it from a laptop: cd docs && python3 -m http.server 8000, then http://localhost:8000/batch.html and scorer.html; or Option B of the beginners walkthrough and the Python scorers
